brief: Three bases arranged around an empty spot, with a bay tray standing in that spot.

requirements.requirement: Three bases arranged around an empty spot
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases at level 0, cells (1,0), (1,-1) and (0,-1), surround the empty cell (0,0) on three flats. The cell (0,0) holds no base.

requirements.requirement: A bay tray standing in that empty spot
requirements.evidence: bay:0#0,0#bay0 (hex-bin-bay-s-full-solid, south-hand full bay tray) at cell (0,0), offered by find_sockets and accepted by the configurator. Bay was refused in other three-base layouts (alternating neighbours, mutually touching triangle) and only seats where the three bases are consecutive around the spot.
capOpenFaces and lockJoints applied (11 end caps, 2 joint bolts); check_build ok with no issues and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built three full hex bases at (1,0), (1,-1) and (0,-1) on level 0 with an empty cell at (0,0) between them, and a full solid south-hand bay tray seated in that empty cell. Open faces are capped and joints bolted. check_build is clean with meshClash clear. I did not add props, since the brief is about structure only.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
